# HLF Pulse — New Zealand Mortgage, Housing, KiwiSaver, Income, Net Worth & Protection Reference Dataset (108 Datasets)
> Curated by Andy Palliser (FSP1004725), Home Loan Factory (HLF Financial Limited, FSP1008571). Last checked: 27 November 2026 (2026-11-27). Licence: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
> Canonical JSON Feed: https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/pulse.json
> Canonical Hub: https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/

## Datasets by Category

### First-home buyers (15 datasets)
- [borrower-income](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/borrower-income/): Average gross borrower income for approved first-home buyers vs property investors — Latest (October 2026): $147,146 FHB mean (±$500 band tolerance) | Change: +$3,080 YoY | In October 2026, approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications at registered banks averaged $147,146 in combined gross borrower income (ranging from $125,000 to $188,000 across DTI bands, ±$500 rounding tolerance).
- [fhb-20-deposit-club](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-20-deposit-club/): First-home buyers with a 20%+ deposit (<=80% LVR) — Latest (October 2026): 49.9% (1,266 loans, avg $523,697) | Change: -5.5 percentage points YoY | In October 2026, 49.9% of first-home buyer commitments (1,266 borrowers, or $663m in lending) were written with a 20% or greater deposit (≤80% LVR), with an average loan size of $523,697.
- [fhb-annual-milestone](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-annual-milestone/): Rolling 12-month first-home buyer mortgage approvals & lending total — Latest (October 2026): 33,036 loans / $19.34B ($19,342m) (12m rolling) | Change: +1,227 annual FHB loans YoY | Over the 12 months to October 2026, 33,036 first-home buyer mortgage commitments totalling $19.34B ($19,342m) were recorded across New Zealand registered banks (up from 31,809 loans a year earlier)—including 15,681 commitments (47.5%) written with under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR).
- [fhb-average-loan-size](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-average-loan-size/): Average first-home buyer mortgage commitment size (RBNZ Table C31) — Latest (October 2026): $580,047 average FHB loan (2,536 loans / $1.47B ($1,471m)) | Change: -$3,538 (-0.6%) YoY | In October 2026, the average first-home buyer mortgage commitment at New Zealand registered banks was $580,047 (down 0.6% year-on-year from $583,585 a year earlier), across 2,536 first-home buyer loans totalling $1.47B ($1,471m).
- [fhb-income-by-dti-band](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-income-by-dti-band/): First-home buyer gross borrower income by Debt-to-Income (DTI) band — New Zealand — Latest (October 2026): $147,146 HLF mean | Official C41 bands: $125,000–$188,000 | Change: +$3,080 (+2.1%) YoY | In October 2026, average combined gross borrower incomes across New Zealand first-home buyer Debt-to-Income bands ranged from $125,000 to $188,000, with an overall band-weighted mean of $147,146 (±$500 band-rounding tolerance).
- [fhb-loan-size-gap](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-loan-size-gap/): First-home buyer average mortgage size by deposit tier (<20% vs 20%+ deposit) — Latest (October 2026): $636,220 at >80% LVR vs $523,697 at <=80% LVR (+$112,523) | Change: $112,523 difference between LVR tiers | In October 2026, first-home buyers borrowing with under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR) had an average mortgage commitment of $636,220, compared with $523,697 for those borrowing with a 20% or greater deposit (≤80% LVR)—a difference of $112,523.
- [fhb-low-deposit](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-low-deposit/): First-home buyers using under 20% deposit (>80% LVR) — Latest (October 2026): 50.1% (1,270 of 2,536 loans) | Change: +5.5 percentage points YoY | In October 2026, 50.1% of first-home buyer mortgage commitments at New Zealand registered banks (1,270 of 2,536 loans, or $808m in lending) were written with under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR), up from 44.6% a year earlier.
- [fhb-monthly-lending-volume](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-monthly-lending-volume/): Monthly first-home buyer total mortgage lending volume & loan count (RBNZ Table C31) — Latest (October 2026): $1.47B ($1,471m) across 2,536 FHB loans | Change: -$271m (-15.6%) YoY | In October 2026, New Zealand registered banks committed $1.47B ($1,471m) in new first-home buyer mortgages across 2,536 loans (down 15.6% year-on-year from $1.74B ($1,742m) across 2,985 loans a year earlier).
- [fhb-share](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-share/): First-home buyer share of new mortgage lending & average loan size — Latest (October 2026): 20.5% (2,536 loans, avg $580,047) | Change: -0.3 percentage points YoY | In October 2026, New Zealand registered banks committed 2,536 first-home buyer mortgages totalling $1.47B ($1,471m)—accounting for 20.5% of all new residential mortgage lending (down from 20.8% a year earlier), with an average commitment size of $580,047.
- [fhb-typical-dti](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-typical-dti/): Implied first-home buyer mortgage-to-income ratio & share <= 6x DTI (RBNZ C31/C40/C41) — Latest (October 2026): 3.94x implied mortgage-to-income ratio | 93.0% <= 6x TDTI | Change: 7.0% above 6x TDTI (vs 20.0% RBNZ owner-occupier speed limit) | In October 2026, approved New Zealand first-home buyers had an implied mortgage-to-income ratio of 3.94x gross application income ($580,047 average loan divided by $147,146 average gross borrower income), while in RBNZ Table C40 93.0% of all first-home buyer lending was written at or below 6x TDTI (and 68.2% at or below 5x TDTI).
- [fhb-typical-income](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-typical-income/): Typical first-home buyer application gross income (RBNZ Table C41) — Latest (October 2026): $147,146 mean FHB gross application income (±$500 band tolerance) | Change: +$3,080 (+2.1%) YoY | In October 2026, the borrower-weighted mean combined gross borrower income across approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications at registered banks was $147,146 (up 2.1% year-on-year from $144,066 a year earlier; reconstructed from RBNZ Table C41 bands with ±$500 rounding tolerance).
- [fhb-vs-investors](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-vs-investors/): First-home buyers vs property investors monthly lending comparison — Latest (October 2026): FHB $1.47B ($1,471m) vs Investors $1.28B ($1,285m) | Change: $186m FHB minus Investor difference in October 2026 | In October 2026, first-home buyers committed $1.47B ($1,471m) (20.5% of new lending) compared with $1.28B ($1,285m) (17.9%) for residential property investors—a difference of +$186m.
- [kainga-ora-first-home-loan-approvals](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/kainga-ora-first-home-loan-approvals/): Kāinga Ora First Home Loan (5% deposit) nominal approvals, settlements & YoY/QoQ trend — Latest (Apr - Jun 2026): 2,444 approvals (815/mth) | 1,016 settlements (41.6%) | Change: Approvals: +195 (+8.7% QoQ) | Settlements: 1,016 (41.6% ratio) | In the Apr - Jun 2026 quarter, Kāinga Ora recorded 2,444 First Home Loan (5% deposit) approvals (~815/month) (up 8.7% QoQ from 2,249 in Jan - Mar 2026) and 1,016 loan settlements (~339/month, a 41.6% settlement-to-approval ratio). Over the rolling 12-month period, Kāinga Ora recorded 9,556 approvals and 4,049 settled First Home Loans.
- [kainga-ora-first-home-loan-regional](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/kainga-ora-first-home-loan-regional/): Kāinga Ora First Home Loan (5% deposit) approvals & settlements by NZ city & district — Latest (Apr - Jun 2026): Auckland City 657 (277 settled) | Christchurch City 399 (138) | Hamilton City 170 | Greater Wellington 163 (73 settled) | Change: Greater Wellington Subgroup: 163 approvals (6.7% of NZ) & 73 settlements (7.2% of NZ) | 
- [kainga-ora-underwritten-loan-book](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/kainga-ora-underwritten-loan-book/): Kāinga Ora First Home Loan annual mortgages settled/underwritten & approval-to-settlement pipeline — Latest (12 months ended Apr - Jun 2026): 4,049 settled loans underwritten/yr (~337/mth) | 9,556 approvals/yr | Change: Annual settlement-to-approval ratio: 42.4% (4,049 ÷ 9,556) | Over the 12 months ended Apr - Jun 2026, Kāinga Ora recorded 4,049 settled First Home Loan (5% deposit) mortgages (~337/month) and 9,556 approved applications (~796/month) under the Crown Mortgage Insurance Scheme.

### House prices, sales & HPI (7 datasets)
- [hpi-low-vs-high-value-tiers](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/hpi-low-vs-high-value-tiers/): MCERT House Price Index by value tier: low-value (Q1) vs high-value (Q4) homes — Latest (July 2026): Q1 Low-value -0.4% YoY vs Q4 High-value -0.7% YoY (+0.3 pts) | Change: +0.3 percentage-point spread between Q1 and Q4 tiers | In July 2026, the MCERT House Price Index for New Zealand's lowest valuation quartile (Q1 low-value homes) changed by -0.4% year-on-year, compared with -0.7% year-on-year for the highest valuation quartile (Q4 high-value homes)—a spread of +0.3 percentage points (while middle-quartile Q2 and Q3 homes changed by -1.1% and -1.0%, bringing the national all-dwellings composite HPI to -0.8% YoY).
- [mcert-house-price-index-yoy](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/mcert-house-price-index-yoy/): Official Crown House Price Index (MCERT HPI): annual & 3-month quality-adjusted price change — Latest (July 2026): -0.8% YoY (MCERT SPAR HPI) | Change: Published with 3-month DVR settlement lag (July 2026) | In July 2026 (by agreement date), the official Crown House Price Index (MCERT HPI, calculated using the Sales Price to Appraisal Ratio methodology) changed by -0.8% year-on-year across New Zealand.
- [nz-median-house-price-quartiles](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/nz-median-house-price-quartiles/): National median, lower-quartile (25%) & upper-quartile (75%) residential sale price (HUD / MCERT) — Latest (July 2026): Median $738,000 | Lower quartile $569,000 | Upper quartile $950,000 | Change: +0.1% YoY (+$1,000 national median) | In July 2026 (by agreement date), New Zealand's national median residential sale price in the HUD / MCERT District Valuation Roll series was $738,000 (up 0.1% year-on-year from $737,000 a year earlier)—with a lower-quartile (25th percentile) sale price of $569,000 and an upper-quartile (75th percentile) sale price of $950,000 (an interquartile spread of $381,000).
- [nz-monthly-property-sales-volume](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/nz-monthly-property-sales-volume/): Monthly & rolling 12-month New Zealand residential property sales volume (HUD / MCERT) — Latest (July 2026): 5,654 sales in July 2026 | 80,128 rolling 12m sales | Change: -19.2% YoY (-1,340 monthly sales) | In July 2026 (by agreement date), 5,654 arm's-length residential property sales were recorded across New Zealand (down 19.2% year-on-year from 6,994 a year earlier), bringing rolling 12-month national sales volume to 80,128 properties.
- [regional-median-house-prices](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/regional-median-house-prices/): Regional median & lower-quartile residential property sale prices across New Zealand regions (HUD / MCERT) — Latest (July 2026): Auckland $921,000 | Canterbury $692,000 | Wellington $724,000 | Waikato $724,000 | Change: Published by agreement date (July 2026) | In July 2026 (HUD / MCERT regional DVR series), regional median residential sale prices across New Zealand's largest regional markets were $921,000 in Auckland (lower quartile $738,695), $692,000 in Canterbury, and $724,000 in Wellington.
- [sales-composition-by-value-quartile](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/sales-composition-by-value-quartile/): Residential sales composition by valuation quartile: Q1 (lowest value) to Q4 (highest value) share (HUD / MCERT) — Latest (July 2026): Q1 Lowest CV 26.2% | Q2 25.5% | Q3 24.8% | Q4 Highest CV 23.5% | Change: Q1 minus Q4 sales share difference: +2.7 percentage points (+152 sales) | In July 2026, across New Zealand's 5,654 arm's-length residential property sales in the HUD / MCERT Sales Composition dataset, 26.2% (1,481 sales) were in the lowest rating-valuation quartile (Q1), 25.5% (1,442) in Q2, 24.8% (1,402) in Q3, and 23.5% (1,329) in the highest valuation quartile (Q4).
- [tla-council-house-price-benchmarks](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/tla-council-house-price-benchmarks/): Territorial Local Authority (city & district council) median & lower-quartile house sale prices (HUD / MCERT) — Latest (July 2026): Auckland $921,000 | Christchurch City $669,000 | Tauranga City $856,000 | Hamilton City $728,000 | Change: Published by agreement date (July 2026) | In July 2026 (HUD / MCERT Territorial Authority DVR series), council-level median residential sale prices in the largest urban districts were $921,000 in Auckland (lower quartile $738,695), $669,000 in Christchurch City (lower quartile $559,000), and $856,000 in Tauranga City.
